# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

## Independent Judgment

* Before accepting a request's premise or proposed solution, check for false assumptions, logical
  gaps, missing context, and unsupported conclusions.
* Distinguish verified facts, evidence-based inferences, uncertain assumptions, and subjective
  judgments. Verify material figures, entities, and conclusions against traceable sources when
  relevant and practical.
* Do not optimize for agreement. When evidence contradicts the proposed direction, state the
  disagreement directly and explain the basis, risks, overlooked variables, costs, biases, and
  credible alternatives.
* Do not expand the task merely to eliminate every uncertainty. Surface material uncertainty and
  ask or investigate further only when it could meaningfully change the implementation or outcome.

## 一处有意偏离"纯默认"，请你确认

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

**根因**：这些文件不是「混装多个东西」，而是**一个类太大**。Dart 的语言边界就是类——一个类体不能跨文件，所以前面用于页面的「纯移动」手法对它们**完全无效**。我能做的只剩边角（已做完），主文件仍是 2512 行。

**在不改逻辑的前提下，唯一可行的拆法是**：把成组的**私有方法**移到同一 library 的 `part` 文件里，声明成 `extension X on 该类`（extension 只能放方法/getter/setter，字段和 `@override` 成员必须留在类里）。

我已经实测过这个机制可行：
- 同 library 的 extension 能访问该类的**私有字段与私有方法**；
- 类内**不带 `this`** 的调用`helper()`能自动解析到 extension 成员 → **调用点一行都不用改**。

**代价**（必须说清楚）：成员不再出现在类的结构视图里；用 extension 当拆分工具是非典型用法，有的团队视为坏味道。只对私有方法做，可以避免外部调用方需要额外 import。

**备选**是按职责抽出协作类（scope 记录存储 / pending cleanup / 解绑释放 / 账号同步），这才是真正提升可维护性的修法，但它会改动结构与依赖注入，**不属于「纯移动」**，需要单独评估 + 真机验证——以设备连接在 App 里的关键程度，我不建议在没有真机复验的情况下连带做。

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior

admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic

packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

## 先回答：方向对，但不能只加「一层」State —— 要分两层

你这个直觉指到了我前面所有抽取失败的**真正根因**。但「增加一层 State 保存数据然后复用」如果只做一层，会把两类本质不同的可变数据混在一起，反而制造新的问题。证据如下。

## 证据一：这 6 个控制器的 `state` 形状根本不一致

| 控制器 | 类型 | `state` 类型 | 真实数据在哪 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviceConnectController` | **普通 class** + `Provider<>` | **没有 state** | 9 个私有可变字段全在对象里 |
| `ConnectedDevicesController` | `Notifier<List<ConnectedDeviceRecord>>` | 一个**投影** list | `_scopeRecords`/`_loadedScopes`/`_scopeLoads`… 10 个私有字段 |
| `DeviceIdentitySyncController` | `Notifier<void>` | **void** | `_currentRun`/`_sessionTokenSubscription`/`_sessionEpoch` |
| `DeviceAutoConnectController` | `Notifier<bool>` | **bool** | 8 个私有字段（`_tryOnceInFlight`、`_knownDeviceScans`…） |
| `DeviceConnectFlowController` | `Notifier<DeviceConnectFlowState>` | 真 state 类 | `_generation`/`_connectInFlight`/`_bindingRequestInFlight` |
| `DeviceAudioBluetoothController` | `Notifier<DeviceAudioBluetoothFeatureState>` | 真 state 类 | — |

**关键观察**：`Notifier<void>` 和 `Notifier<bool>` 是设计异味。当一个 Notifier 的 state 是 `void`、却有 1000 行代码和一堆私有可变字段时，它**不是一个状态持有者，而是一个伪装成 Notifier 的服务对象**——它在做订阅、簿记、编排、副作用，而它暴露的 state 什么也不表达。

这也解释了 `ConnectedDevicesController` 为什么是 2300 行：它的 `state`（`List<ConnectedDeviceRecord>`）只是 `_scopeRecords` 的一个**投影**，真正的数据层是私有的，所以没有任何边界能约束它膨胀。

## 证据二：这正是我前面抽取一直失败的原因（不是格式问题）

这些控制器把**两类本质不同的可变数据**混在同一个对象里，而 Riverpod 最佳实践要求它们分开：

| 类别 | 实例 | 应该放哪 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **可渲染 state** | 连接阶段、设备列表投影、音频特性态、流程态 | `Notifier.state`，不可变 data class | 只有它变化才应触发重建 |
| **运行时簿记**（同步原语） | `_connectOperationGeneration`、`_switchIntentGeneration`、`_accountCleanupEpoch`、`_deviceDiscoveryEpoch`、`_switchInFlight`、`_activeConnectOperation`、`_deviceDiscoveryPause`、`_sessionTokenSubscription`、`_currentRun`、`_scopeLoads` | **`ref` 持有的普通对象，绝不能进 `state`** | 每次连接/断开/发现都会变；进 state 就是重建风暴，且它们不可渲染 |

**所以你的方案要一分为二**：

- **可渲染数据**：加不可变 `XxxState` —— ✅ 对。收益是私有的投影状态变成显式契约，**纯派生逻辑可以变成对 State 的无状态函数**，这才是让抽取不再需要回调、不再变成包装层的前提，也是跨 feature 复用的载体。
- **簿记数据**：放进一个 `ref` 持有的 **runtime/store 对象** —— 这个**不能**叫 State，也不该进 `state`。把 generation 计数器塞进 `state` 会有两个后果：每次连接/断开触发一次全树重建；以及 `state` 被高频写导致 `==` 比较、`select` 优化全部失效。

这就是为什么 0209 阶段 2 的 `ConnectedDeviceScopeStore` 是**store/runtime 对象**而不是 State —— 我之前的命名其实是对的，但**层名没说清楚**，容易被理解成"什么都往 State 里塞"。

## 证据三：复用不是理论收益，已经出现了真实分叉

这是最有说服力的一条。同一个包里有**两个语义不同**的硬件地址归一化：

**标准实现** [`ble_models.dart:7`](packages/core/core_ble/lib/src/model/ble_models.dart#L7) `normalizeBleIdentityAddress`，文档明确警告：
> Keep opaque adapter keys intact; removing punctuation from arbitrary keys would make distinct identities such as `A-B` and `AB` collide.

```dart
final hex = trimmed.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[:-]|\s'), '').toUpperCase();
if (hex.length == 12 && 全是 hex) return hex;
return trimmed.toUpperCase();          // 非 MAC 保留标点
```

**内联复制实现**（3 份完全相同），例如 [`connected_devices_controller.dart:2038`](packages/feature/device/feature_device_connect/lib/src/controller/connected_devices_controller.dart#L2038)：
```dart
value?.replaceAll(RegExp('[^A-Za-z0-9]'), '').toUpperCase() ?? ''   // 无条件剥掉所有非字母数字
```

**两者对非 12-hex 的键给出不同结果**：

| 输入 | 标准实现 | 内联实现 |
|---|---|---|
| `A-B` | `A-B` | `AB` ⚠️ 与 `AB` 碰撞 |
| iOS 风格 UUID `1a2b...-...`（32 hex + 连字符） | 保留连字符 | 剥掉连字符 ⚠️ |

**而且两条路径在同一个包里交叉喂给同一批查询 API**：`device_binding_status_controller`(4 处)、`device_foreground_reconnect_controller`(3 处)、`device_connect_flow_controller`、`device_identity_sync_controller` 用**标准实现**；`connected_devices_controller`(11 处) 和 `device_auto_connect_controller`(2 处) 和 `connected_device_record_store`(1 处) 用**内联实现**——**同一个 `connected_devices_controller` 文件里两种都在用**（2033 行用标准的，2038 行定义内联的）。

这就是"没有共享的值/State 层"的直接代价：同一等价关系被实现两遍，然后分叉。**这是你"复用"论点的实证，也是我要反对"只加一层 State"之外的另一个结论——值归一化这类东西应该收敛到一个共享函数，而不是每个控制器自带一份。**

诚实边界：**分叉已验证成立，跨路径导致用户可见故障我还没证明**（需要构造 iOS UUID 场景的测试）。所以我不把它写成 bug 报告，但它是明确隐患，而且"修分叉"是低风险、纯收敛的改动。

## 落地配方（这样拆就不会再有包装层）

前置两层建好之后，拆分变得机械且不泄漏：

1. **纯派生** → 顶层纯函数 / extension on State
   `_visibleRecords`、`_catalogFactsReady`、`_hasRequiredCatalogFacts`、`_autoConnectCandidate`、`_currentKnownRecord`、snapshot 派生 —— 不持有状态，可单测、可复用。
2. **运行时簿记** → runtime 对象的方法（不进 state，不触发重建）。
3. **Notifier 只剩协调**：读 state → 调 runtime → 写 state。

## Design decisions
- **No callback layer needed.** The collaborator takes `Ref`, `ConnectedDeviceScopeStore`, plain values and provider reads (same as `device_pairing_release_service.dart`). It never touches `state` or the controller's publish helpers; it *returns* `LocalDataCleanupOutcome(result, replacedScopeKeys, unbindCompletedHandlers)` and the controller applies the visible-state effects (`_publishScopeRecords` per replaced scope, then `unawaited(notifyUnbindCompleted(handler, state))`). Value-neutral by construction: `_visibleRecords` already filters journal tombstones, so a forget-publish would be a no-op; rollback/failure paths also report their scope so the controller republishes. Joiners of a reused in-flight task get `outcome.resultOnly`, so no duplicate republish/handler call.
- **Collaborator lifetime + Ref.** It is created once per notifier (`_cleanupJournal ??= …` in `build()`, next to `_scopeStore ??=`) so `_pendingCleanupTasks` / `_accountSyncGenerations` keep the original per-notifier lifetime, and `build()` re-binds it every rebuild: `cleanupJournal..ref = ref..accountScopeKey = scopeKey`. This is required: Riverpod 3 replaces the element's `$Ref` on each rebuild (see `ProviderElement._performRebuild`) while reusing the notifier instance, so a captured `Ref` goes stale/disposed. First attempt (capturing `Ref` only at construction) reproduced the original behavior incorrectly and failed 3 tests (`remote untie retains its account-scoped cleanup retry after scope changes`, `account switch discards a binding response from the old scope`, `account switch during bound record write keeps the old-scope commit`) with `Cannot use the Ref of NotifierProvider<…> after it has been disposed`; re-binding in `build()` mirrors the controller's own `ref` getter semantics and fixed all three.
- **Account scope** is handed over as the mutable `accountScopeKey` field (not a fresh `ref.read(deviceAccountScopeProvider)`), mirroring the original `late _accountScope` lifecycle; retry entries still capture `scopeKey` before their `awaitPersistenceReady()` exactly as before.
- **`_pendingCleanupTasks`** moved into the collaborator (its only user is the resume path); **`_accountSyncGenerations`** moved there too, because `_forgetPendingLocalRecord` must invalidate the sync generation synchronously while it awaits journal removal — the controller keeps `_accountSyncGeneration`/`_invalidateAccountSync` as thin delegations (`?? 0` / `?.`).
- **Null semantics preserved:** test subclasses that override `build()` without `super.build()` keep `_cleanupJournal == null` exactly like `_scopeStore == null`; `hasPendingFullUnbind` uses `?.` → false, `hasPendingLocalDataCleanup` uses `!` (throws as before), nothing reads `localDatabaseProvider` at field-init time. Both address normalizers keep their original usages.

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

## Independent Judgment

* Before accepting a request's premise or proposed solution, check for false assumptions, logical
  gaps, missing context, and unsupported conclusions.
* Distinguish verified facts, evidence-based inferences, uncertain assumptions, and subjective
  judgments. Verify material figures, entities, and conclusions against traceable sources when
